title: Soft abelian sheaves on paracompact spaces are acyclic
statement: Let $X$ be a paracompact Hausdorff topological space, where paracompact means that every open cover admits a locally finite open refinement. Let $G$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on its open-subset site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Assume that $G$ is soft: for every closed subset $S\subseteq X$, the restriction map $\Gamma(X,G)\to\Gamma(S,i^{-1}G)$ is surjective, where $i:S\hookrightarrow X$ is inclusion with the subspace topology and $i^{-1}G$ is the sheaf of locally represented germs of $G$ along $S$. Then $H^r(X,G)=0$ for every integer $r>0$, where $H^r=R^r\Gamma(X,-)$ is computed in abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology].

source.place: WANTED locally; read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf. IV §4, Definition (4.9), Proposition (4.14), Theorem (4.15), printed pp.204--205, applied to the closed subset X itself.

proof.text: Fix $X$. We prove the assertion for all soft abelian sheaves on $X$, by induction on the positive degree. The opens of $X$ form a set-sized site (intersections give the covering pullbacks). By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives], embed an arbitrary soft $G$ into an injective abelian sheaf $I$. In that abelian category take the cokernel $Q$, giving $0\to G\to I\to Q\to0$.

The sheaf $I$ is flasque [def-sc-zariski-flasque]. To apply [lem-sc-ringed-space-injective-restriction-surjective], give $X$ the sheaf $\mathbf Z_X$ of locally constant integer-valued functions. Every abelian sheaf has a unique $\mathbf Z_X$-module structure: on an open where the integer function is $m$, act by repeated addition by $m$, and glue. Every abelian-sheaf morphism respects this action, since it respects integer multiples locally. Thus the module and abelian-sheaf categories have the same objects and morphisms under this identification; the extension property defining injectivity is identical. Apply the cited restriction theorem to $I$ as an injective $\mathbf Z_X$-module, for every pair of nested opens.

source.place: Tag 01EA (lemma-injective-restriction-surjective), equivalently Tag 09SX (lemma-injective-flasque), for the ringed space (X, Z_X)

proof.text: For any closed $S\subseteq X$ and $s\in\Gamma(S,I|_S)$, [lem-sfb-closed-section-neighborhood-extension] gives an open $U\supseteq S$ and $t\in I(U)$ restricting to $s$. Flasqueness [def-sc-zariski-flasque] gives $\widetilde t\in I(X)$ restricting to $t$. Its restriction to $S$ is $s$. Hence $I$ is soft. This proves the entire flasque-to-soft implication directly from the cited extension statement.

source.place: IV §4, Corollary (4.8) and Example (4.10), printed p.204

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-soft-kernel-closed-sections] to $0\to G\to I\to Q\to0$. The two first sheaves are soft, so $Q$ is soft. Taking the closed subset $S=X$ in its lifting assertion shows that $\Gamma(X,I)\to\Gamma(X,Q)$ is surjective.

Global sections is additive and left exact, and $H^q=R^q\Gamma(X,-)$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] to the short exact sequence. Since $I$ is flasque, [lem-sc-topological-flasque-acyclic] gives $H^q(X,I)=0$ for all $q>0$. The segment $\Gamma(X,I)\to\Gamma(X,Q)\to H^1(X,G)\to H^1(X,I)=0$ and Step 4 give $H^1(X,G)=0$. For $q\ge1$ the segment $0=H^q(X,I)\to H^q(X,Q)\xrightarrow{\delta^q}H^{q+1}(X,G)\to H^{q+1}(X,I)=0$ makes $\delta^q$ bijective.

source.place: IV §4, Theorem (4.15), assembled as in the proof of (4.4); long exact sequence IV (3.5); Stacks Tag 09SY (lemma-flasque-acyclic)

proof.text: The base degree $1$ holds for every soft $G$ by Step 5. Suppose degree $q\ge1$ vanishes for every soft sheaf on $X$. For an arbitrary soft $G$, its quotient $Q$ from Steps 1--4 is soft, so $H^q(X,Q)=0$ by the induction hypothesis. The bijection of Step 5 gives $H^{q+1}(X,G)=0$. Induction proves the assertion for every positive integer degree.

source.place: IV §4, Theorem (4.15), explicit induction underlying the resolution argument

split_report.summary: Expanded Demailly IV (4.15) into an injective dimension-shifting proof, retaining the exact statement. Used the existing ringed-space injective restriction theorem via the explicit locally constant integer action, and the existing closed-section neighborhood-extension and flasque-acyclicity nodes. Created only Proposition (4.14), a genuine lifting/quotient lemma, as a statement-only child. Searched the current DAG, latest blueprint, project Lean and Mathlib; recorded actual searches and exact citation quotes.

tool_uses.why: Generic injective-sheaf restriction theorem, specialized to the locally constant integer sheaf; the unit has no separate restriction theorem.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q25-666980ada (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: The item is still unsplit live, with the same statement and stmt_deps, so no other group has superseded it; this is a first split, not a re-split. Demailly is not available locally, so the item and the new node were checked against the structure of Demailly IV (4.9), (4.14), (4.15), together with Stacks 01EA, 09SX and 09SY. Steps: (1) enough injectives on the opens site, then a cokernel; (2) ℤ_X-module identification, and the restriction node needs only a ringed space, not a locally ringed one, which matters because the stalks of ℤ_X are ℤ; (3) flasque implies soft through the neighborhood-extension node, with the same paracompact Hausdorff hypotheses; (4) the new node gives that Q is soft and, with S=X, that Γ(I)→Γ(Q) is onto; (5) the long exact sequence plus flasque acyclicity, with H^0=Γ by def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology (2); (6) the induction is set up properly, base case q=1 and step q to q+1 over all soft sheaves. New node lem-sfb-soft-kernel-closed-sections is statement-only and self-contained, and is the (4.14) lifting lemma, strictly smaller than the item rather than a restatement. A scan of the DAG for soft/flabby/paracompact found no duplicate. Small cases checked: a point, S empty, S=X, A=0, and the constant sheaf ℤ on [0,1] (not soft, so the hypothesis does real work). Accepted tool_uses: injective restriction, flasque acyclicity, derived long exact sequence. No changes.
